response: According to the available data, hospitals may provide lower quality care on weekends, particularly for elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Research suggests that weekend hospitalization can lead to delayed provision of intensive procedures and elevated 1-year mortality rates for these patients. This raises concerns about the efficacy of certain regulations, such as mandated nurse staffing ratios, in enhancing the quality of weekend care. Instead, targeted financial incentives might be a more cost-effective policy response to improve the quality of care on weekends.
